clue.text: Expressing sympathy with wife taking out small dog

indicators.note: the wife comes in and takes out the small one, so one letter replaces another in the word

parts.note: saying sorry expresses sympathy
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
W is the genealogical abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Someone consoling a wife whose little dog has been taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small dog' reads as a pet, but 'small' is S and 'dog' is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to pester or harass them persistently, as a terrier harries its prey.

clue.text: It was extravagant also to purchase black belt

indicators.note: also takes hold of black, purchase meaning grip, so the two sit together
extravagant means wild or wandering, so the letters stray into a new order

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: Splashing out on a martial arts black belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extravagant' rearranges IT WAS to WAIST; 'to purchase' sets B beside AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A waistband is the strip of a garment that encircles the waist, effectively a belt.

clue.text: One getting up right after unconfined craving returns

indicators.note: the right comes after the rest
returns says the trimmed word comes back, read in reverse
unconfined means without its outer edges, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: a craving is a strong desire

explanation.surface: Someone getting up once a strong urge comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unconfined' strips DESIRE to ESIR, which 'returns' reverses to RISE.
explanation.definitionFit: An early riser is someone who gets out of bed, i.e. gets up.

clue.text: Longed having base for trophy made

indicators.note: in a down clue the base of a word is its bottom, that is final, letter

parts.note: earned and made both mean gained as income

explanation.surface: Desperate to win, having built a plinth for the cup.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn is to long for something with deep desire.

clue.text: Student is man primarily behind museum defacement

indicators.note: the student, is and the man's first letter come behind (after) the museum

parts.note: V AND A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London, usually written V&A
L is the learner driver's plate, standing for a student

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A student and a man are blamed for vandalising a museum exhibit.
explanation.walkthrough: The V&A (the Victoria and Albert Museum in London) is spelt out with AND in full.
explanation.definitionFit: Defacing property deliberately is a classic act of wanton destruction by hooligans.

clue.text: Covert manoeuvres to find carrier of disease

indicators.note: manoeuvres says the letters are moved around into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Secret operations to track down a disease source.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a vector is an organism, like a mosquito, that transmits a pathogen.

clue.text: Reportedly sees gang as symbol of teenage rebellion?

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said aloud, so the spoken words give the answer

parts.note: sees means knows, as in understands, and a gang is a ring

explanation.surface: Someone spots a gang and takes it for teenage defiance.
explanation.walkthrough: KNOWS RING said aloud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A piercing through the nostril is a typical teenage gesture of defiance; the question mark flags it as an example.

clue.text: Fruit in part damaged, one firm to cut

indicators.note: to cut means the extra pieces slice into the shuffled letters
damaged says the word part is broken and its letters rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Some fruit was partly bruised, one company having to trim it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges PART to APRT, and 'to cut' places ICO inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The apricot is a small orange stone fruit.

clue.text: Entering computer data at home before golf practice

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in
putting is rolling the ball towards the hole on the green, often practised

explanation.surface: Typing in data at home before some time on the putting green.
explanation.definitionFit: Inputting is feeding information into a computer, keying it in.

clue.text: Ideal shape

definitions.meaning: to form or mould something, a verb

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a perfect exemplar and the act of sculpting something into form.

clue.text: Examples of current attitudes

parts.note: something current is in, as in fashionable
attitudes or positions taken are stances

explanation.surface: Cases illustrating present-day opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like electricity (AC or I) but here it means fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Instances are individual cases cited as illustrations, i.e. examples.

clue.text: Quick run followed by a bath when back

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

indicators.note: when back says the word for bath is read from right to left

parts.note: a dip is a quick bathe

explanation.surface: A quick jog, then a dip once you get home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when back' sounds like returning home but reverses DIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid and quick are straightforward synonyms for fast-moving.

clue.text: City entertained by actor on tour

indicators.note: the city is held inside the words that follow, the way a guest is entertained by a host

explanation.surface: A touring actor performs to a city's audience.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the largest city in Canada, capital of Ontario.

clue.text: Article about music performance

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece on a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a concert given by a soloist or small group.

clue.text: Intimate description of naturists perhaps, nothing originally omitted

indicators.note: omitted says a letter is left out of the phrase

parts.note: naturists might be described as all nude

indicators.note: originally means only the opening letter of nothing is used

explanation.surface: An intimate account of nudists, with nothing left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intimate' looks like an adjective (close) but is the verb, to hint.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimate is to suggest indirectly, which is what referring obliquely to something does.

clue.text: Two houses sharing same area as public buildings

indicators.note: sharing the same letter means the two words overlap, so one copy is dropped

parts.note: Libra and Aries are two houses (signs) of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Two homes using one plot as civic buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' are zodiac signs, not dwellings; the two signs overlap on a single A.
explanation.definitionFit: Public lending libraries are municipal buildings open to all.

clue.text: Hobby that might lead to numerous rows?

definitions.text: Hobby that might lead to numerous rows?

parts.words: Hobby that might lead to numerous rows?
parts.note: rows sounds like quarrels, but the pastime produces row after row of stitches

explanation.surface: A pastime that causes lots of arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' reads as fights (to rhyme with 'cows') but means lines of stitches (to rhyme with 'goes').
explanation.definitionFit: Working wool with needles builds a garment up one row of stitches at a time.

clue.text: Fame of criminal sergeant loathes ultimately

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent, so the letters are twisted out of order
ultimately means only the very last letter of loathes is taken

explanation.surface: A corrupt sergeant's notoriety, which he ultimately hates.
explanation.definitionFit: Greatness is eminence or distinction, close in sense to renown.

clue.text: Short comedian upset person honoured with distinction

indicators.note: short means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: Stan Laurel was the thin half of the comedy double act Laurel and Hardy
ate means upset or troubled, as in what's eating you

explanation.surface: A distressed little comic upset the award-winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' suggests a small comedian but trims LAUREL to LAURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A laureate is someone awarded a high honour, such as a Nobel prize winner.

clue.text: Discovered woman's bred unusual dog

indicators.note: unusual says the letters are put into an unusual order
dis-covered means with its cover, the outside letters, stripped off

explanation.surface: It turns out a woman has bred an odd-looking hound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' looks like 'found out' but strips W and S from 'woman's', leaving OMAN; with BRED that is shuffled by 'unusual'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dobermann is a breed of guard dog, named after its German breeder.

clue.text: Earthenware pots initially rejected for garden feature

indicators.note: initially rejected means the first letter is thrown out

parts.note: crockery is earthenware dishes and pots

explanation.surface: Clay pots first turned down for a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A rockery is an arrangement of stones with alpine plants in a garden.

clue.text: Hit for one making record

definitions.meaning: in cricket a stroke that scores one run is called by this name
a disc with one track on each side, released on its own

explanation.surface: A batsman's one-run shot sets a new record.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket shot worth one run shares its name with a one-song record.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a one-run stroke and a stand-alone song release take the word meaning 'only one'.

clue.text: Hearing occasionally news about huge blaze

indicators.note: about means going around, so the news surrounds the other letters

parts.note: info is information, news

indicators.note: occasionally means every other letter of hearing is picked

explanation.surface: A court hearing gets sporadic coverage of a huge fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' looks like a court session but just gives its even letters ERN.
explanation.definitionFit: An inferno is a raging, intense fire.

clue.text: Good musical instrument to take up for free

indicators.note: in a down clue taking up means reading the word upwards, i.e. reversed

parts.note: the sitar is an Indian stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A decent instrument to take up for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take up' sounds like starting a hobby but reverses SITAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratis is Latin-derived for without charge.

clue.text: Comparatively rare extract from Oscar ceremony

indicators.note: extract from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rare clip from the Academy Awards night.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarcer is the comparative of scarce, meaning harder to find or less plentiful.

clue.text: Crowd is passionate supporting Wales at last

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means placed beneath
at last means only the last letter of Wales is taken

parts.note: warm means ardent or passionate

explanation.surface: A crowd is fervently cheering on Wales at last.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarm is a dense moving crowd, as of bees or people.

clue.text: Consider to turn back

definitions.meaning: as a mirror sends light or an image back

explanation.definitionFit: One word means both to ponder deeply and to throw back light, as a mirror does.

clue.text: Demand legislation relating to divorcees?

definitions.meaning: to insist on and obtain, as to extract a payment
a whimsical reading: an act of parliament for former spouses

explanation.surface: Calling for a law on divorced couples.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the jokey second reading: former partners plus a statute.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact a price is to demand it; read in two parts it is a law for former partners.

clue.text: Like swimmer being apart from others

parts.note: as means like, in the sense of in the manner of
the ide is a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: A lone swimmer keeps away from the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmer' suggests a person but is a fish, the ide.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand aside is to be off to one side, separate from everyone else.

clue.text: Every second adult bird departed, circling round

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: circling round says one word goes around the other

parts.note: the late are those who have died, i.e. departed
the tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Each second an adult bird flies off, then circles back.
explanation.definitionFit: Alternate as an adjective means every other one, one on and one off.

clue.text: Mother's welcoming American publicity for traditional British food

indicators.note: welcoming means taking the other pieces in

parts.note: ma is mother, plus the S of the possessive
hype is aggressive publicity or promotion

explanation.surface: Mum embraces American promotion of an old-fashioned British dish.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a side dish of mashed marrowfat peas, served with fish and chips in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft mashed marrowfat peas are a classic British side dish, eaten with fish and chips.

clue.text: Vows of loyalty he's regularly disregarded

indicators.note: every other letter is ignored, so the remaining alternate letters spell the answer

explanation.surface: His pledges of allegiance are routinely ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping L, Y, L, Y and E from 'loyalty he's' keeps the second, fourth and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath is a solemn promise, a vow sworn formally.
